entries.title: Kuva Larvling
entries.summary: Finish it, and your Lich is born
items: kuvalich:kuva_larvling_spawn_egg

blocks.text: Tenno, bring it down and it will show you your future nemesis's weapon. End it, and the Lich will wake.

The <hl>{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_larvling}</hl> is a Lich that has not grown up yet. While you have no Lich, one turns up near you every so often. The weapon your future Lich will carry is settled the moment it appears: which weapon, its level and its element, all revealed once you knock it down. Finish it, and your own {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} is born, coming for you alone from then on.
When it comes

items: It only comes to players without a Lich; once you have one, no more Larvlings come for you

One comes every <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMinMinutes}-{cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMaxMinutes}</t> minutes you spend online; the timer pauses while you are offline and picks up when you return. Only one at a time
It usually appears <t>16-28</t> blocks away, somewhere out of your sight, and charges at you, with a notice reading “{lang:message.kuvalich.larvling.appeared}”
It doesn't come while you are in a dimension it doesn't go to, on Peaceful, or in Creative or Spectator, nor in your first <t>30</t> seconds after joining
While it is still on its feet, if you get more than <t>96</t> blocks away, change dimension, log out or die, it dissolves, and another comes <t>2</t> minutes later

blocks.text: How your Lich is born

items: Knock it down: it has only <t>70</t> health, easier than a Thrall. A lethal blow doesn't kill it; it goes <w>down</w> for <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingDownedSeconds}</t> s

Check the weapon it reveals: once it is down, it shows your future Lich's weapon with its level and element. That is the weapon your Lich will carry, and the one you earn when you finally end it, level and element unchanged. If you don't like it, let it go and wait for the next one
Get within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyReach}</t> blocks and look at it; when “{lang:kuvalich.mercy.prompt.larvling}” appears, press the <t>{lang:key.kuvalich.mercy}</t> key (default <t>X</t>)
When the execution finishes it dissolves into Kuva, and your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} is born and speaks to you for the first time

blocks.text: Kill it with your own hands and your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master} is born, carrying the weapon settled when it appeared, level and element included. The killing blow must come from a player who has no Lich yet; one finished off by a pet, another mob or lava gives nothing.

blocks.title: Execute it in time
blocks.text: Once a Larvling is down, nothing can hurt it: more gunfire or blows do nothing, and only a Mercy finishes it. If no one executes it within {cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingDownedSeconds} seconds, it dissolves on the spot. A dissolved Larvling gives nothing, and the next one is {cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMinMinutes}-{cfg:kuva_lich.larvlingIntervalMaxMinutes} minutes away.
Who can execute it

items: Players who already have a Lich can't execute a Larvling, and knocking one down for someone else doesn't take it from them
The executor is decided the moment it goes down: if the player who downed it (a pet counts as its owner) has no Lich yet, it is theirs
Otherwise it belongs to the player it came for, as long as they are online, in the same world and still without a Lich; if neither fits, no one can execute it and it dissolves when its timer runs out
So if a friend without a Lich knocks your Larvling down, the Lich is born on their side; a friend who already has one can help you down it and you keep the claim

blocks.text: In the Origin System, a Kuva Larvling shows up mid-mission and, once downed, reveals its future Lich's weapon, bonus element and Ephemera. You can Mercy it to make it your nemesis, or simply leave it be.
Details

items: <t>70</t> health, <t>5</t> attack, <t>2</t> armor, <t>0.33</t> speed; damage uses the Thrall formula (attack × difficulty factor × 0.85), and like a Thrall it takes a flat <t>×0.75</t> damage and counts as undead
It drops nothing and gives no decryption progress
It is never saved: when the world is closed or its chunk unloads before it is downed, it simply leaves, and another comes <t>2</t> minutes later

items.text: Once a Larvling has been down, however it ends (a Lich born or timed out), the next one takes a full wait

items: Larvlings from spawn eggs work too: finish one while you have no Lich and you get a Lich all the same

entries.title: Kuva Thrall
entries.summary: Your everyday foe: progress, materials, mods
items: kuvalich:kuva_slave_spawn_egg

blocks.text: Mere Thralls. Dying in my place is all they are good for.

The answer that ends a Lich has to be dug out of its Thralls, one at a time, Tenno. The <hl>{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}</hl> is the foot soldier of the Kuva enemies and the one you meet most. Every one you put down brings you a step closer to hunting your {lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}, and it may leave materials and mods behind.
<dim>Names like “Kuva”, “Lich” and “mod” come from Warframe. If they are new to you, see the [[start/glossary|glossary]].</dim>
When they come

rows: Only players who already have a Lich; without one, first finish off a [[enemies/kuva_larvling|Kuva Larvling]]

A squad every <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadIntervalMinSeconds}-{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadIntervalMaxSeconds}</t> s, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadSizeMin}-{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadSizeMax}</t> Thralls each; the timer starts over when your Lich is born and when you log in
<t>16-28</t> blocks from you, out of sight, close together, and they charge you as soon as they land
No squad comes while <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadMaxNearby}</t> Thralls are already within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallSquadRadius}</t> blocks of you; near the cap, fewer come
While you are in a dimension they don't go to, on Peaceful, in Creative or Spectator, or in the middle of an execution
They don't stay: walk far away and they despawn like ordinary monsters

blocks.text: How it fights

items: Hits hard: Easy <t>6.8</t>, Normal <t>13.6</t>, Hard <t>20.4</t> per hit
A hit <w>launches you</w>, while the Thrall lunges after you and heals <t>0.8</t>
Half again as fast as a zombie; it comes for you once it sees you within <t>32</t> blocks
Regenerates slowly, <t>1</t> health per second, or <t>0.5</t> with no target
Picks fights with other monsters nearby, even neutral ones such as Endermen, and spares only Creepers and other Kuva enemies

items.text: The longer the fight, the harder it hits, see [[enemies/battle_boost]]

blocks.text: Base stats

rows: <t>Undead</t>, but it does not burn in sunlight like zombies
Shown within <t>16</t> blocks: once you have a Lich, it reads your Lich's name followed by “Thrall”; until then, “{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_slave}”. Just the name, no health bar

blocks.text: Because it is undead, Smite and the “{lang:item.module.bane_of_undead}” stat on mods work against it, and Healing and Harming potions work the other way round.
Downed and executed

items.text: A lethal hit does not kill it; it goes <w>down</w> instead: no moving, no attacking, no healing, and its battle boost freezes
A lethal hit does not kill it; it goes <w>down</w> instead: no moving, no attacking, no healing

items: Only whoever knocked it down can execute it: one you downed is yours, one a pet or summon downed belongs to its owner, and one finished by a fire or lava you caused is yours too

Get within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyReach}</t> blocks and look at it; when “{lang:kuvalich.mercy.prompt.thrall}” appears, press the {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy} key (default <t>X</t>; at that moment X counts only as Mercy and won't also trigger anything else bound to it). An execution takes about <t>2.2</t> seconds
You cannot be hurt during an execution and cannot do anything else; once it ends you can move straight on to the next
You cannot execute a Thrall someone else downed; up close you only see “someone's quarry”
If nobody executes it within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds}</t> seconds, it fades away and leaves nothing; so does one downed by another mob, which nobody is entitled to execute
Only executed Thralls give decryption progress and drops

blocks.text: Drops

items: Enough <t>decryption progress</t> reveals, one by one, the Requiem cards you need to beat the Lich (see [[requiem/decryption]]); once all three clues are revealed, kills stop adding progress

items.text: <t>Decryption progress</t> isn't only for whoever finishes it: when it falls, every player with a Lich within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.thrallProgressShareRange}</t> blocks gets the same amount; drops and Lich rage go to the finisher alone

items: Players without a Lich get no decryption progress

<t>Mods</t> are upgrade cards you fit to a weapon or to yourself (see [[modules/module_overview]]). <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleWeaponRatio|pctv}</t> of dropped mods are weapon mods, and the rest are Warframe mods, which go on you
The three mod tiers share a single roll, so at most one mod drops per kill; see [[modules/module_rarity]] for the tiers
Kuva, Riven Slivers and Requiem Gems each roll independently; see [[start/materials]] for their uses

blocks.title: You must land the killing blow
blocks.text: Weapons, arrows and thrown items all count as yours. A kill by a pet, another mob or lava does not count, and neither does burning to death, even from your own Fire Aspect or Flame arrows. In those cases you get no progress and no drops.
Thralls are a Lich's underlings, found across the territory it holds. Finishing them off slowly reveals the Requiem mods needed to defeat their master; here, that became decryption progress.
Deep intel

items: Damage formula: 8 × difficulty factor × 0.85, where the factor is 1 on Easy, 2 on Normal and 3 on Hard. When it hits you, vanilla applies its own difficulty scaling on top, and armor comes after that
Knockback strength: your horizontal speed ×3, vertical ×2

items.text: Elemental kills don't count either; a killing blow from {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} burn or from {lang:kuvaweapon.type.poison}, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.gas}, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity} or {lang:kuvaweapon.type.explosion} damage gives you nothing (see [[combat/elements]])

items: Requiem Gems only check Looting on the item in your main hand at the moment it pays out; Fortune does nothing, and a bow in your main hand counts as Looting 0
These drops are spawned directly where it fell, so the “{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.itemDropMultiplier}” stat on Warframe mods does not boost them

entries.title: Kuva Lich
entries.summary: The boss: how to meet it and what winning gives you
items: kuvalich:kuva_master_spawn_egg

blocks.text: The <hl>{lang:entity.kuvalich.kuva_master}</hl> is the boss, waiting at the end of the Requiem decryption road. Each player has exactly one: it is born when you finish off a [[enemies/kuva_larvling|Kuva Larvling]], and from then on it comes for you alone. The progress you built and the card order you worked out are all put to the test on this creature of the Queens, Tenno; do not falter here. Guess right, and the Kuva weapon it carries is yours.
The hunt, step by step

items.text: Knock down a [[enemies/kuva_larvling|Kuva Larvling]] and execute it; your Lich is born, carrying the weapon the downed Larvling revealed, with the same level and element
Kill a [[enemies/kuva_larvling|Kuva Larvling]] yourself; your Lich is born, carrying the weapon settled when the Larvling appeared

Execute Thralls to build [[requiem/decryption|decryption progress]] and reveal the answer clue by clue. Each <t>clue</t> is one <t>Requiem card</t> of the answer, and three cards in the right order are the password that defeats the Lich

Kill Thralls to build [[requiem/decryption|decryption progress]] and reveal the answer clue by clue. Each <t>clue</t> is one <t>Requiem card</t> of the answer, and three cards in the right order are the password that defeats the Lich

items: Put three cards, in the order you guess, into the [[requiem/requiem_gate|Requiem Gate]], the block made for holding them

items.text: Wait for its rage to fill and for it to come to you, or call it with a {item:kuvalich:requiem_ultimatum}
Wait for its rage to fill and for it to come to you

Its health comes in three segments, and it goes down each time one empties. Execute it with {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy}: the 1st time is 1 stab checking card 1, the 2nd is 2 stabs checking the first two, and only three right stabs on the 3rd end it. Any wrong stab and it breaks free and escapes, with [[enemies/kuva_escalation|Lich rank]] +1
Kill it; the answer is checked the moment it falls. Right means rewards; wrong and it escapes, with [[enemies/kuva_escalation|Lich rank]] +1

blocks.text: The creature above is what the records call a Kuva Lich, a nemesis unique to each Tenno. Only by fitting three Requiem mods to the Parazon and finishing it with them in the right order is it ended for good, and its Kuva weapon taken.
How it finds you

You do not go looking for it, Tenno; it comes looking for you. Once its rage is full, it sets out after <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichArrivalDelayMinSeconds}~{cfg:kuva_lich.lichArrivalDelayMaxSeconds}</t> seconds; how its rage builds is covered in [[requiem/lich_archive]].

items.text: It speaks over the comm first and appears about <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichCommLeadTicks|sec}</t> later
It speaks over the comm first and appears right after

It appears <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichSpawnMinDistance}~{cfg:kuva_lich.lichSpawnMaxDistance}</t> blocks away, somewhere out of your sight, and its boss bar appears at the top of the screen at the same time: name, rank badge and health, three thin segments lit for the clues you have revealed, and a row beneath showing its adaptation stacks and [[enemies/battle_boost|battle boost]]

It appears <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichSpawnMinDistance}~{cfg:kuva_lich.lichSpawnMaxDistance}</t> blocks away, somewhere out of your sight, and its boss bar appears at the top of the screen at the same time: name, rank badge and health, three thin segments lit for the clues you have revealed, and a row beneath showing its adaptation stacks

items: It targets only you and can chase you within <t>96</t> blocks. If someone else hits it, it turns on them, but after a while it comes back for you
Only one comes for you at a time; it does not use portals and never despawns like an ordinary mob
Its nameplate shows within <t>32</t> blocks, and other players also see whose Lich it is

items.text: A {item:kuvalich:requiem_ultimatum} calls it straight to you; see [[requiem/requiem_items]]

blocks.text: How it talks over comms, and how it fights, both come from the <t>personality</t> it was born with. A jovial Lich laughs a lot and calls you "friend"; it hits hard, is fragile and grows fiercer by the second. A logical Lich is cold and terse and calls you "opponent"; it is tough, heavily armored and adapts fast. The personality is fixed at birth, and each Lich also rolls its own weaknesses, resistances and ability strengths, see [[enemies/lich_traits]].

How it talks over comms depends on the <t>personality</t> it was born with. Some are jovial: they call you “friend” and keep joking even as they lose. Others are cold and logical: they call you “adversary” and speak as if passing a verdict. The personality is fixed the moment it is born and only changes what it says, not how strong it is.
When it holds off

A full rage bar does not always bring it at once. In the cases below it waits and sets out as soon as the condition clears; the status line in the [[requiem/lich_archive]] says what it is waiting for.

items: You are in a dimension it does not hunt in (<t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichHuntDimensions|list}</t>)
Peaceful difficulty

items.text: You are in Creative or Spectator mode
You are sleeping, riding, executing, or dead
You are sleeping, riding, or dead
You logged in less than <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichLoginGraceSeconds}</t> seconds ago

blocks.text: When it leaves
Every encounter ends with its rage back at zero, and it waits at least <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichCooldownMinutes}</t> minutes before coming again. Any of these makes it leave:
Every encounter ends with its rage back at zero. Any of these makes it leave:

items: You get more than <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichLeashDistance}</t> blocks from it, change dimensions or log out
You die

items.text: No blows pass between you for <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichIdleDepartSeconds}</t> seconds, and nobody else hits it either

items: The difficulty is set to Peaceful

items.text: A wrong stab, and it breaks free and escapes
A wrong card order when it is killed, and it breaks free and escapes

If you do not execute it within {cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds} seconds of it going down, it refills that segment and gets back up to fight on; only after 3 downs in a row go unexecuted does it escape in a Kuva mist, leaving nothing

items: What leaves is the same Lich, and it will be back; the round only ends when you end it

blocks.text: Base stats

cells: At rank 2, about <t>170</t> for a jovial Lich and <t>240</t> for a logical one, varying a little per Lich, see [[enemies/lich_traits]]

Max health × <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichShieldRatio}</t>; damage hits the shield before health. It starts recharging after <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichShieldDelaySeconds}</t> s without being hit, at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichShieldRegenPercent|pctv}</t> of the cap per second; a hit that empties it makes the wait × <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichShieldBrokenDelayMultiplier}</t>. It refills whenever the Lich breaks loose from an execution and stands. While the shield holds, {lang:kuvaweapon.type.magnetic} status makes it take far more damage; see [[combat/element_status]]
<t>0.35</t>; jovial ones are <t>8%</t> faster, logical ones <t>5%</t> slower

rows: <t>64</t> blocks, <t>96</t> while it is hunting you
Fire and falling, so burning, lava and {lang:kuvaweapon.type.fire} elemental burn can't hurt it

blocks.text: How it fights

items.text: It hits harder: one blow = attack × difficulty factor × 0.85, with attack about <t>15.6</t> for a jovial Lich and <t>11</t> for a logical one, so about <t>26.5</t> / <t>18.8</t> per blow on Normal. "Per blow" in the [[requiem/lich_archive]] shows exactly how hard yours hits you
Hits even harder: Easy <t>11.05</t>, Normal <t>22.1</t>, Hard <t>33.15</t> per hit
A hit <w>sends you flying</w> and heals it: <t>20%</t> of its attack at average strength, <t>10%</t> weak, <t>30%</t> strong, <t>45%</t> as its signature
A hit <w>sends you flying</w> and heals the Lich <t>2.6</t>

It regenerates every second: <t>2</t> health or <t>2%</t> of missing health with a target, whichever is larger, and <t>1</t> or <t>1%</t> without one; its regeneration strength multiplies that by <t>0.5–2.2</t>
It regenerates every second: with a target, <t>2</t> or <t>2%</t> of missing health, whichever is larger; without one, <t>1</t> or <t>1%</t>
The longer the fight, the harder it hits, see [[enemies/battle_boost]]

items: Your damage against it has to get through several reduction layers first, see [[enemies/lich_resistance]]

blocks.title: It spares no one
blocks.text: Its attacks are <w>area attacks</w>: every swing deals the same damage to every other creature within <t>2.5–4.5</t> blocks of its body (depending on its quake strength, shown in the archive); only Kuva enemies are spared. It does not tell friend from foe, and every life you bring along is within its reach.

blocks.title: It spares no one
blocks.text: Its attacks are <w>area attacks</w>: every swing also deals the same damage to every other creature within <t>3</t> blocks of its body, and only Kuva enemies are spared. It strikes without regard for friend or foe, and everything you bring is within its reach.
Downed and executed

items: Its health bar has <t>three segments</t>, and it goes <w>down</w> each time one empties: no moving, no attacking and no further damage, and its boss bar turns grey, while that segment slowly refills as the downed timer runs
It does not matter who lands that hit; people helping you can knock it down too, but only you can execute it, and anyone else up close only sees “someone's quarry”

Get within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyReach}</t> blocks and look at it; when “{lang:kuvalich.mercy.prompt.lich}” appears, press the {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy} key (default <t>X</t>; at that moment X counts only as Mercy and won't also trigger anything else bound to it)

You cannot be hurt during the execution and cannot do anything else. The 1st down takes <t>1</t> stab checking card 1 only, the 2nd takes <t>2</t> checking the first two, and the 3rd takes <t>3</t>; stabs always check from position 1 on and stop at the first wrong one
If every stab is right on the 1st or 2nd execution, it breaks loose and stands with the next segment full, and the fight goes on; only three right stabs on the 3rd end it

If you do not act within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds}</t> seconds of it going down, the segment refills and it stands to fight on; after <t>3</t> unexecuted downs in a row it escapes, leaving nothing
Damage such as <t>/kill</t> or falling into the void kills it outright without downing it; the encounter is void and gives nothing

blocks.title: Before the first stab
blocks.text: If an execution is interrupted before the first stab lands, it is void and the Lich stays down where it was, with at least <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyResumeFloorSeconds}</t> seconds left; once the first stab has landed, an interruption settles the result on the spot.

blocks.title: Before the first stab
blocks.text: If an execution is interrupted before the first stab lands, it is void and the Lich stays down where it was, its downed timer still running; once the first stab has landed, an interruption settles the result on the spot.
Judged on the kill

items: When it falls, your cards are judged no matter who landed the last hit, so people helping you never spend your three cards for you
You must be online, in the same world and within <t>64</t> blocks of it; otherwise there is no judgement, you get nothing, and it comes back later

blocks.text: The outcome

cells: Fewer than 3 cards in the Requiem Gate
Still judged stab by stab; an empty slot among the ones checked this time counts as wrong: a decryption failure, same as “any wrong” below
Fewer than 3 cards in the Requiem Gate
No judgement: it dissolves and leaves, and you get decryption progress, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.masterPotionMultiplier|x}</t> a Thrall's

rows: <g>Decryption succeeds</g>: it is ended, you get the rewards below, and a new round starts
Decryption fails: it breaks free and escapes, [[enemies/kuva_escalation|Lich rank]] +1, and you still gain progress

items: On success, progress and clues are all cleared and the next round's answer is rolled anew; your next Lich is born when you finish off another [[enemies/kuva_larvling|Kuva Larvling]], and your Lich rank starts over at 1
On failure, chat tells you where the cards started going wrong; see [[requiem/decrypt_failure]] for how to test orders

blocks.text: Rewards for a successful decryption

rows: 1, the very weapon it carries, at the level and element the Larvling revealed when it went down
1; needed to craft three workstations, see [[requiem/requiem_items]]
Always 1, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.masterPrimeModuleChance|pctv}</t> <c:55FFFF>Prime</c> and otherwise <c:FF55FF>Riven</c>; <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.moduleWeaponRatio|pctv}</t> of them are weapon mods
Each loses 1 durability; survivors return to your inventory, see [[requiem/requiem_cards]]
Minimum and maximum both rise, see below

items: <c:55FFFF>Prime</c> and <c:FF55FF>Riven</c> are two advanced mod tiers; see [[modules/module_rarity]] for how they differ

The minimum and maximum of your weapon level range both rise by the same random amount, <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.minimumLevelCapIncrease}-{cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevelCapIncrease}</t>; the minimum caps at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.minimumLevel}</t> and the maximum at <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.maximumLevel}</t> (see [[weapons/weapon_level]])
This kill's Kuva weapon was settled from the range before the increase when the Larvling appeared; the new range applies from your next Larvling

blocks.text: <w>Don't finish it next to lava or the void</w>. Except for the Requiem cards that go back to your inventory, every reward drops where the Lich fell, and so do cards that don't fit in your inventory.

blocks.title: Ownerless Liches give nothing
blocks.text: A Lich released from a spawn egg or by command has no owner: no nameplate or boss bar, no downed state, and killing it judges nothing, gives no progress and drops nothing at all.

blocks.title: Ownerless Liches give nothing
blocks.text: A Lich released from a spawn egg or by command has no owner: no nameplate or boss bar, and killing it judges nothing, gives no progress and drops nothing at all.
Deep intel

items: Its damage formula is attack × difficulty factor × 0.85, the same as Thralls
Knockback strength: horizontal ×3.15, vertical ×2.15

items.text: The “{lang:item.module.execute_threshold}” and “{lang:item.module.execute_chance}” stats only knock it down when they trigger; ending it still takes your execution

If it cannot reach you for more than <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichRepositionSeconds}</t> seconds, it shifts through a Kuva mist to a hidden spot near you, at most <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichRepositionMax}</t> times per encounter

items: It is never saved: if its chunk unloads or the world closes, it simply leaves and the encounter ends as usual
Liches never spawn naturally, and spawners cannot produce them
Rewards are spawned straight onto the ground, so the “{lang:kuvaweapon.warframe_attribute_type.itemDropMultiplier}” stat on Warframe mods does not boost them

entries.title: Lich Rank
entries.summary: Each wrong guess adds a rank; only success resets it

blocks.text: Every wrong guess stays on your record until you get it right. Your <hl>Lich rank</hl> keeps that count: your Lich is born at rank 1 and gains 1 with every failed judgement, chat shows the new rank, and the rank badge in the [[requiem/lich_archive]] and on its boss bar changes with it.

items: The rank is stored on you and belongs to this round's Lich
Dying does not reset it; only a successful decryption clears it, and the next Lich starts again at 1

items.text: In an execution an empty slot counts as a wrong guess too, so an incomplete set still raises the rank
Going after it with an incomplete set is not a wrong guess; you only get progress

blocks.text: Strike off the mark, Tenno, and I take my leave. Ha. Your blade is quicker than your wits.
What an interesting move, friend.
What it does to you
From rank 2 on, each rank adds <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.increaseDamage|pct}</t> to the damage Kuva enemies deal to you, meaning Thralls and Liches. Damage from other mobs, falls and lava is unaffected.

header: Damage Kuva enemies deal to you

blocks.text: From rank 2 on, each rank also cuts your damage to Kuva enemies by <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.reducedDamage|pct}</t>, up to 99.9%; other targets are unaffected.
Your Lich rank only counts wrong guesses and does not weaken you; a wrong guess only costs you a success.
Its effect on the Lich

The Lich itself changes with rank too: its health and armor are based on rank 2 and gain <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichRankHealthStep|pct}</t> per rank, capped at rank <t>6</t>; a newborn rank 1 Lich has that much less. Its attack does not grow with rank.

blocks.title: Swap cards after a wrong guess
blocks.text: A wrong guess does not take your three cards; they stay in the [[requiem/requiem_gate|Requiem Gate]] that holds them. Leave them as they are and the same wrong set fails again, for another +1 rank. Change them before it comes for you again, and don't let one mistake cost you twice.

To find the right order in as few tries as possible, see [[requiem/decrypt_failure]]; the execution record in the [[requiem/lich_archive]] keeps which positions were right and wrong in your recent tries.

Operator, the archives say finishing a Lich with the wrong Requiem sequence fails; it survives the blade, ranks up and grows stronger. Here, the rank is kept on you instead. A Lich that slips the blade a rank stronger, Ordis would <x>feed to the engines-- slowly-- GRIND to dust--</x> pardon. That half need not be filed.

entries.title: Lich Personality and Stats
entries.summary: Jovial or logical: weaknesses, resistances and ability strengths differ for every Lich

blocks.text: Every Lich is born with a <hl>personality</hl>. It decides not only how the Lich talks over comms but also how it fights. The exact numbers are in the [[requiem/lich_archive]]: its personality sits under its name, the stats list its health, armor, how hard one blow hits you, its weaknesses and resistances, and the dots under the ability icons show their strength.

items: Weaknesses and resistances are drawn among melee, arrows, other projectiles and magic; the remaining types stay unchanged. A melee resistance never goes below ×0.85, so a blade alone still works
Attack does not grow with rank; health and armor follow the [[enemies/kuva_escalation|Lich rank]], and the table shows rank 2

blocks.text: Ability strength

Each of the five abilities is weak, average or strong. Half of the abilities its personality favors come out strong, and half of the ones it disfavors come out weak. Every Lich also has one <hl>signature</hl> ability, stronger still, whose icon has a red outline in the archive.

cells: +{cfg:kuva_lich.battleBoost|mul:1.6|pct} per second, winds down half as fast without a target

rows: 45%, plus a share for everyone its heavy blow sweeps

blocks.title: How to deal with it
blocks.text: A jovial Lich is fragile but grows fiercer fast: prepare for its weaknesses and <g>end it quickly</g> before its fury builds. A logical one is tough and adapts fast: <g>bring several damage types and keep rotating</g>. More in [[enemies/lich_tactics]].

entries.title: Battle Boost
entries.summary: The longer a fight lasts, the harder they hit

blocks.text: No need to rush, my little adversary. In my sector, I can afford to wait... you may not.
Kuva enemies get fiercer as a fight drags on. <hl>The longer the fight, the more damage they deal</hl>, with no cap, so finish them fast.
Damage dealt by Kuva enemies × (1 + seconds in combat × {cfg:kuva_lich.battleBoost|pct})
How the timer works

items: Every Thrall and Lich keeps its own timer

It starts <w>the moment it locks on</w>, not when blows are exchanged: a Thrall locks on when it sees you within <t>32</t> blocks, your own Lich locks onto you the moment it appears, and an ownerless Lich locks on when it sees you within <t>64</t>
It keeps climbing as long as it has a target, whether that is you, your pets or a mob it is fighting
Without a target it counts back down at the same rate, so after 60 seconds of fighting it takes 60 seconds out of combat to reach zero

items.text: How fast your Lich builds up depends on its fury strength: <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.battleBoost|mul:0.6|pct}</t> to <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.battleBoost|mul:1.6|pct}</t> per second, as shown in the [[requiem/lich_archive]]; one with fury as its signature also winds down half as fast after losing its target

items: A Thrall's timer is saved with it; unloading and reloading the chunk does not clear it

items.text: While it is down, the timer freezes, neither rising nor falling

blocks.title: Fury you can see
blocks.text: The longer a fight runs, the brighter the Kuva veins on a Lich glow; drag it out further and red embers keep rising off its body while a dark red haze seeps from its feet. Your own Lich's boss bar shows the current boost beneath it. Thralls that have fought for a while give off red motes from the sacs on their backs. The brighter the veins and the thicker the embers, the harder it hits.

entries.title: Lich Resistances
entries.summary: Why your damage falls off: four layers, one by one

blocks.text: If your damage on a Lich keeps shrinking, you are not imagining it, Tenno; its defenses are built in layers. Every hit you land on a Kuva enemy passes through several reduction layers first; Thralls have the first two, the Lich has all four.

cells: Thralls and wild Liches: arrows ×1.25, other projectiles and magic ×0.75. Your Lich: two weaknesses and one resistance if jovial, one weakness and two resistances if logical, with its own multipliers
Repeated hits of one damage type, -3% to -7% per stack, up to 4–6 stacks depending on its adaptation strength
Repeated hits of one type stack -5% each, up to -30%

rows: The more hits within 2 seconds, the less each does, down to 40%
The part above <t>15%</t> of max health is heavily compressed

blocks.title: Only raw damage is reduced
blocks.text: These layers only reduce the hit's raw damage, made up of weapon attack damage, enchantments and jump crits. Mod stats, mod crits and elemental multipliers are applied after the layers, so the soft cap never touches them; see [[combat/damage]].
1. Damage type modifier

rows: It was hit directly by an arrow, such as a bow arrow, a crossbow bolt or a thrown trident
Any other damage counted as a projectile, such as snowballs or projectiles from other mods
Potions, Thorns and other magic damage, plus spells from other mods that are recognized as magic
A living creature hit it directly, which covers your own swings and the attacks of pets and summons
Anything not listed above, such as explosions, lightning or burning

blocks.text: Types are checked from the top row down, and the first match wins. Layer 2 keeps separate stacks for these same five types.

blocks.title: Every Lich is different
blocks.text: When your Lich is born it rolls its weaknesses and resistances among melee, arrows, other projectiles and magic: a jovial Lich gets two weaknesses (×1.25–1.40) and one resistance (×0.75–0.85), a logical one gets one weakness (×1.25–1.40) and two resistances (×0.60–0.75); the rest stay unchanged, and a melee resistance never goes below ×0.85. The [[requiem/lich_archive]] lists its weaknesses and resistances. Thralls and wild Liches follow the table above.
2. Adaptive resistance (Lich)
The Lich adapts to how you fight. The more you use one damage type, the harder that type gets cut.

items: Each of the five types keeps its own stacks
Each hit is first reduced by that type's current stacks, <t>5%</t> per stack, and then that type gains one more, so the first hit goes through in full
Stacks cap at 6, which is -30% for that type
A type that lands no hit for <t>4-5</t> seconds loses a stack, then one more every <t>5</t> seconds
After more than <t>10</t> seconds without taking any damage, every type resets to zero

items.text: Those are the numbers at average strength. Your Lich follows its adaptation strength: weak is <t>3%</t> per stack, at most <t>4</t> stacks, losing them after <t>3</t> seconds; strong is <t>6%</t> per stack; as its signature it is <t>7%</t> per stack and keeps each stack for <t>6</t> seconds, see [[enemies/lich_traits]]

blocks.text: Don't let it learn your pattern. <g>Rotate damage types</g>. Use melee for a while, switch to the bow, then to spells, and let the idle types shed their stacks. <w>A new weapon is not a new type</w>; two swords are both melee and share one counter.

Ordis's records hold a Warframe mod called Adaptation: taking damage of one type builds resistance to that type. The Lich's adaptive resistance runs on the same idea, only this time it is the enemy who learns.
3. Burst diminishing (Lich)
The more hits it takes in a short time, the less each one hurts.
Damage multiplier = max(40%, 1 − hits already taken in the last 2 seconds × 5%)

blocks.title: What counts as a hit
blocks.text: <w>Every hit that actually lands counts</w>, and every one adds a stack: each tick of {lang:kuvaweapon.type.poison} or {lang:kuvaweapon.type.gas} damage over time, the extra {lang:kuvaweapon.type.electricity} or {lang:kuvaweapon.type.explosion} damage, Thorns, your pets' attacks, even uncharged swings. The more damage over time you bring, the lower your main hits sink.
4. Soft damage cap (Lich)
When a single hit is too big, the excess is heavily compressed, so the higher your weapon's own attack damage, the harder it gets squashed.
Threshold = max health × 15% (default 200 × 15% = 30); above it: damage = threshold + ln(1 + excess × 0.5) ÷ 0.5

header: Hit after the first three layers

blocks.title: Its defenses show
blocks.text: These layers all show themselves. An arrow hit bursts a star of golden cracks across its body; adaptive resistance raises a hexagon plate on the side that was struck, more solid with every stack; and when burst diminishing or the soft cap cuts a big share, a white cross of light and a spray of sparks burst from the point of impact with a dull clang. Your own Lich's boss bar shows which damage types have stacks, and how many, in the row of icons beneath it.

blocks.title: Its defenses show
blocks.text: These layers all show themselves. A hit with its weakness bursts a star of golden cracks across its body (for Thralls and ownerless Liches, the weakness is arrows); adaptive resistance raises a hexagon plate on the side that was struck, more solid with every stack; and when burst diminishing or the soft cap cuts a big share, a white cross of light and a spray of sparks burst from the point of impact with a dull clang. Your own Lich's boss bar shows which damage types have stacks, and how many, in the row of icons beneath it.
Deep intel

items: Attacks fully blocked by hit invulnerability do not count as a hit
{lang:kuvaweapon.type.slash} elemental damage over time removes health directly, skipping every layer, adding no stacks and taking no burst slot

items.text: All damage from these mods counts as magic: <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.magicDamageNamespaces|list}</t>

items: For ways around all of these layers, see [[enemies/lich_tactics]]

entries.title: Hunting the Lich
entries.summary: Putting it together: prepare, deal damage, finish

blocks.text: Kneeling is not surrender, Tenno. Do not keep it waiting.
Until it falls for good, do not take your eyes off it, Tenno.

Reductions and boosts all bear down on you at once in a hunt. What I want is a clean finish: prepare before the fight, get around its reductions while you deal damage, and close it out without a slip.
Before the fight

items.text: Check that the three cards in the [[requiem/requiem_gate|Requiem Gate]] are the order you want to test; an empty slot counts as wrong
Check that the three cards in the [[requiem/requiem_gate|Requiem Gate]] are the order you want to test; with fewer than three it is only a progress run

items: Bring at least two or three damage types, such as a melee weapon, a bow or crossbow and spells, and ideally a [[weapons/kuva_weapons|Kuva weapon]] with strong mod multipliers

items.text: Check its personality, weaknesses and resistances in the [[requiem/lich_archive]] first and pick weapons to match

items: When its rage is nearly full, wait somewhere open and flat, away from pets and villagers: its area attack reaches several blocks around it (the quake icon in the archive says how far), and the knockback can throw you off a cliff

items.text: To choose the arena, call it there with a {item:kuvalich:requiem_ultimatum}

blocks.text: Dealing damage

items.text: <g>Bows and crossbows first</g>, since Arrow is the only type with ×1.25 and it stacks separately from melee
<g>Use its weaknesses first</g>: that type takes ×1.25–1.40, and each type stacks separately
Fight to its personality: a jovial Lich is fragile but grows fiercer fast, so finish it before its fury builds; a logical one is tough and adapts fast, so bring several damage types and keep rotating

items: Rotate damage types and switch after a few hits, so no type reaches full stacks
Pacing beats speed. From the 13th hit within 2 seconds you deal only 40%, so one fully charged hit beats two half-charged ones
Keeping each raw hit around <t>15%</t> of its max health (30 at 200 health) is enough; almost everything beyond that is eaten by the soft cap, so invest in module multipliers instead

items.text: <w>Finish fast</w>; its damage keeps rising with every second of combat, +<t>{cfg:kuva_lich.battleBoost|pct}</t> per second (see [[enemies/battle_boost]])

blocks.text: Getting around the resistances

items.text: The “{lang:item.module.execute_threshold}” and “{lang:item.module.execute_chance}” stats knock it straight down when they trigger (see [[reference/weapon_attr_special]])

The “{lang:item.module.execute_threshold}” and “{lang:item.module.execute_chance}” stats kill the target outright when they trigger, and that works on the Lich too (see [[reference/weapon_attr_special]])

items: {lang:kuvaweapon.type.slash} elemental damage over time and the damage-over-time effects of some [[weapons/weapon_list|Kuva weapons]] remove health directly, skipping every layer and adding no stacks or burst hits

blocks.title: With guns
blocks.text: TACZ bullets resolve as Other, at ×1. Each bullet registers as two hits, even when one part deals 0 damage, so burst diminishing and adaptive stacks climb twice as fast. The extra damage from the “{lang:item.module.true_bullet}” stat removes health directly, bypassing the resistances.
Finishing

items: Move in the moment it goes down and finish it with {lang:key.kuvalich.mercy} within <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.mercyDownedSeconds}</t> seconds; you cannot be hurt during the execution
It does not matter what knocks it down, whether teammates, pets or elemental damage over time, but only you can execute it
Don't wander off while it is down; more than <t>{cfg:kuva_lich.lichLeashDistance}</t> blocks away, a dimension change or logging out still makes it leave
Stay within <t>64</t> blocks for the kill; your cards are judged no matter who lands the last hit, and a kill by elemental damage over time counts too
If it falls while you are too far away or offline, there is no judgement and nothing is given
